findings.title: OpenDiscoveryTrace headline success denominator is exactly reconstructible and covers only 127 non-null statuses out of 372 frontier trajectories
findings.observation: The public analysis has 372 frontier trajectories and per-model process metrics n=124 each, but success uses pandas dropna and has n=43/42/42. Therefore the success mean is over 127 non-null values, not 372. The published mean 0.6929133858267716 equals 88/127 exactly; 245/372 success values are null.
findings.scope_guard: This reconstructs the metric denominator, not scientific correctness.

findings.title: The 127 non-null success statuses mix 126 crude ground-truth token-overlap evaluations with one no-conclusion forced failure
findings.observation: Current harness logic sets success from whitespace-token-set overlap >0.3 only when both a final claim and ground_truth are present; a final claim without ground_truth gets success=null; no final claim gets success=false. The fixed task bank contributes 42 executed frontier tasks with ground_truth across the three models, hence 126 heuristic-scored records. Claude has one no-claim record, yielding the 127th non-null false. The serialized verification field is still pending. Medium success_rate=0.0 is therefore driven by that one forced failure among otherwise null success rows, while hard success is entirely null.
findings.scope_guard: Do not describe medium tasks as uniformly failed or the approximately-69-percent headline as 372 completed verifier judgments.

findings.title: Protocol-064 collapse failure reproduces on an additional Gemini hard sample
findings.observation: dd_h01_gemini-3.1-pro is serialized as one conclusion step with zero tool calls, but its raw_response declares a PubMed action and an API action before a final claim. This independently exercises the same declared-action/executed-action coherence failure on another model and difficulty.
findings.scope_guard: This strengthens the observed failure class but still does not assert every OpenDiscoveryTrace record is incoherent.

findings.title: Audit-Closed v0.2.0 improves distribution but does not close the observed static per-trial public-log archive gap
findings.observation: The current release v0.2.0 packages a portable CLI and reproducible profiles, but GitHub release assets are empty. The inspected results directory contains aggregate/result files rather than serialized per-trial transparency logs. Thus the public implementation remains a strong deterministic-log reference mechanism while a zero-execution external auditor still lacks a committed per-trial log bundle in the inspected primary surfaces.
findings.scope_guard: This is limited to the inspected release assets and primary results directory; it is not an exhaustive negative over every possible mirror.

findings.title: Audit-Closed admission arithmetic can be replayed Chat-natively once a transcript is declarative and repository-bound
findings.observation: The public source defines alpha_epoch=total_alpha*(1-decay)*decay^epoch and threshold=candidate_count/alpha_epoch, with acceptance iff the maximum final e-value reaches the threshold. A protocol-local repository-bound transcript with epoch 0, total_alpha .05, decay .5, two candidates and e-values 100/20 statically recomputes alpha_epoch .025, threshold 80, winner candidate_A and accepted=true without package/model execution.
findings.scope_guard: The transcript is synthetic and validates only final decision replay feasibility; a real empirical trial still requires the logged hash chain, commitments, complete evaluations and e-value provenance.

findings.title: Outcome denominator and verifier provenance requires a distinct fail-closed gate
findings.observation: p1-protocol-065 requires population coverage, row-level evaluated/pending/forced-failure classes, exact evaluator identity, recomputable numerator/denominator and explicit disclosure when heterogeneous outcome semantics are aggregated.
